q: The atomic number of carbon is
e: Carbon has 6 protons, so its atomic number is 6.

q: Which gas turns lime water milky?
e: CO₂ reacts with lime water to form milky calcium carbonate.

q: The pH of a neutral solution at 25°C is
e: A neutral solution has pH 7; below 7 is acidic, above is alkaline.

q: Which is a noble gas?
e: Argon is in Group 18, the noble gases.

q: The most electronegative element is
e: Fluorine attracts electrons more strongly than any other element.

q: Moles in 36 g of water (H = 1, O = 16)
e: Moles = mass ÷ molar mass = 36 ÷ 18 = 2.

q: The chemical symbol for sodium is
e: Na comes from the Latin name natrium.

q: An acid turns blue litmus paper
e: Acids turn blue litmus paper red.

q: A solid changing directly to a gas is called
e: Sublimation is solid to gas without becoming liquid first.

q: Which of these is an alkali metal?
e: Potassium is in Group 1, the alkali metals.

q: Rusting of iron requires
e: Rust forms when iron meets oxygen and water.

q: The most abundant gas in air is
e: Air is about 78% nitrogen.

q: The chemical symbol for potassium is
e: Potassium comes from the Latin kalium, so its symbol is K.

q: A neutral oxygen atom (atomic number 8) has how many electrons?
e: A neutral atom has as many electrons as protons, so 8.

q: The usual valency of Group 1 elements is
e: Group 1 atoms lose one electron, so their valency is 1.

q: Which gas is released when zinc reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid?
e: Zn + 2HCl → ZnCl₂ + H₂. Hydrogen burns with a pop.

q: The formula of sulphuric acid is
e: Sulphuric acid is H₂SO₄.

q: Which of these is an alkali?
e: NaOH (sodium hydroxide) is a soluble base, which is an alkali.

q: Rusting of iron needs
e: Iron rusts when both oxygen and water are present.

q: Salt is best obtained from salt solution by
e: Evaporating the water leaves the salt behind.

q: Ammonium chloride can be separated from sand by
e: Ammonium chloride sublimes when heated, but sand does not.

q: The general formula of the alkanes is
e: Alkanes are saturated hydrocarbons with formula CₙH₂ₙ₊₂.

q: The simplest alkane is
e: Methane (CH₄) has one carbon atom.

q: Alkenes contain a
e: The C=C double bond is the functional group of alkenes.

q: How many atoms are in one molecule of ethane, C₂H₆?
e: 2 carbon + 6 hydrogen = 8 atoms.

q: The relative molecular mass of CO₂ (C = 12, O = 16) is
How many moles are in 36 g of water (H = 1, O = 16)?
e: Molar mass of H₂O is 18 g/mol, so 36 ÷ 18 = 2 moles.

q: Avogadro's number is about
e: One mole contains about 6.02 × 10²³ particles.

q: Isotopes of an element have the same number of
e: Isotopes have the same proton number but different neutron numbers.

q: The maximum number of electrons in the first shell is
e: The first shell holds up to 2 electrons.

q: A bond formed by the transfer of electrons is
e: Ionic bonding involves electron transfer, as in sodium chloride.

q: A covalent bond involves
e: Atoms share pairs of electrons in covalent bonds.

q: The pH of a strong acid is closest to
e: Strong acids have a low pH, around 1.

q: Blue litmus paper turns ___ in acid.
e: Acids turn blue litmus red.

q: A catalyst
o: is used up in the reaction
speeds up a reaction and is not used up
e: A catalyst changes the rate without being consumed.

q: During electrolysis, positive ions move to the
e: Positive ions (cations) move to the negative electrode, the cathode.

q: The Haber process makes ammonia from
e: N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃.

q: At constant temperature, if the pressure on a gas is doubled, its volume
e: Boyle's law: pressure and volume are inversely proportional.

q: Temporary and permanent hardness of water are caused by dissolved
e: Calcium and magnesium salts make water hard.

q: Oxidation is the
e: Remember OIL RIG: Oxidation Is Loss, Reduction Is Gain of electrons.

q: Mass of 0.25 mol of NaOH (Na = 23, O = 16, H = 1)
e: M(NaOH) = 40 g/mol, so 0.25 × 40 = 10 g.

q: Volume of CO₂ at s.t.p. produced from 11 g of CO₂ (C = 12, O = 16; molar volume 22.4 dm³)
Percentage by mass of magnesium in MgO (Mg = 24, O = 16)
Concentration of a solution containing 4.0 g of NaOH in 500 cm³ (Na = 23, O = 16, H = 1)
e: 4/40 = 0.1 mol in 0.5 dm³, giving 0.2 mol/dm³.

q: A gas occupies 200 cm³ at 2 atm and constant temperature. Its volume at 4 atm is
e: Boyle's law: P₁V₁ = P₂V₂, so V₂ = 2 × 200 / 4 = 100 cm³.

q: A gas occupies 300 cm³ at 27°C. Its volume at 127°C and constant pressure is
e: Charles's law with kelvin: 300 × 400/300 = 400 cm³.

q: The electronic configuration of the sodium ion, Na⁺ (atomic number 11), is
e: Na loses its 3s electron, leaving 10 electrons as 1s² 2s² 2p⁶.

q: Across Period 3 from sodium to chlorine, the atomic radius generally
e: Nuclear charge increases while shells stay the same, pulling electrons closer.

q: The shape of a water molecule is
e: Two bond pairs and two lone pairs on oxygen give a bent shape.

q: The bond formed when NH₃ combines with H⁺ to form NH₄⁺ is
e: Nitrogen donates its lone pair to H⁺, forming a coordinate covalent bond.

q: The oxidation number of manganese in KMnO₄ is
e: K = +1, four O = −8, so Mn = +7.

q: The oxidation number of chromium in K₂Cr₂O₇ is
During electrolysis of concentrated brine using inert electrodes, the product at the cathode is
e: H⁺ is preferentially discharged over Na⁺, giving hydrogen gas.

q: Mass of copper deposited when 2 A flows for 965 s through CuSO₄ solution (Cu = 64, F = 96500 C)
e: Q = 1930 C = 0.02 mol e⁻; Cu²⁺ needs 2 e⁻, so 0.01 mol × 64 = 0.64 g.

q: A reaction with a negative enthalpy change (ΔH) is
e: Negative ΔH means heat is released to the surroundings.

q: For N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃ (ΔH negative), increasing the temperature will
o: shift the equilibrium to the right
shift the equilibrium to the left
e: Heat favours the endothermic (reverse) direction, lowering NH₃ yield.

q: Which change increases the rate of reaction between marble chips and dilute HCl?
e: Powdering increases surface area, so more collisions occur.

q: The pH of 0.01 mol/dm³ hydrochloric acid is
e: [H⁺] = 10⁻² mol/dm³, so pH = 2.

q: 25 cm³ of NaOH solution is neutralised by 20 cm³ of 0.1 mol/dm³ HCl. The concentration of the NaOH is
e: Moles HCl = 0.002 = moles NaOH; 0.002/0.025 = 0.08 mol/dm³.

q: NaHSO₄ is classified as
e: It still contains a replaceable hydrogen ion.

q: When concentrated H₂SO₄ is added to sugar, the sugar turns black because the acid acts as
e: The acid removes water from sugar, leaving carbon.

q: The allotrope of carbon that conducts electricity is
e: Graphite has delocalised electrons between its layers.

q: Addition of AgNO₃ solution to a solution of a chloride gives a white precipitate that
e: AgCl dissolves in dilute NH₃ by forming a soluble complex.

q: Brass is an alloy of
e: Brass is copper and zinc; bronze is copper and tin.

q: In the extraction of aluminium, alumina is dissolved in molten
e: Cryolite lowers the melting point of alumina for electrolysis.

q: The IUPAC name of CH₃CH₂CH₂OH is
e: Three carbons with -OH on carbon 1 give propan-1-ol.

q: The characteristic reaction of alkenes is
e: The C=C double bond opens to add other atoms.

q: The enzyme in yeast that converts glucose to ethanol and carbon dioxide is
e: Zymase catalyses alcoholic fermentation.

q: Acid rain is mainly caused by atmospheric
e: SO₂ and NO₂ dissolve in rain to form H₂SO₄ and HNO₃.

q: A compound contains 40% C, 6.7% H and 53.3% O by mass (C = 12, H = 1, O = 16). Its empirical formula is
e: Mole ratio 3.33 : 6.7 : 3.33 simplifies to 1 : 2 : 1.
